name: check-then-act-race
explain: Demonstrate Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) lost update races when application code checks balance before updating. Atomic conditional update predicates (UPDATE ... WHERE balance >= amount) prevent concurrent overdrafts.
steps: Simulate two concurrent transactions reading account balance before deducting funds. || Enforce atomic database-level update predicates to reject the second transaction when funds are exhausted.
expect: Atomic conditional write verified: tx1=True, tx2=False, final_balance=30

name: transaction-atomicity-rollback
explain: Demonstrate ACID transaction atomicity across multiple tables. When an invariant fails mid-stream, uncommitted changes roll back completely with zero persistent dirty state.
steps: Execute multi-table ledger and audit log operations inside an atomic transaction. || Trigger a constraint violation and verify that ledger updates and audit entries roll back completely.

name: optimistic-concurrency-control
explain: Implement Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) using an integer version column. Concurrent writes verify that the row's version matches the version read; stale overwrites affect zero rows and raise 409 Conflict.
steps: Read row revision and submit conditional update asserting matching version. || Verify that a concurrent update based on a stale revision affects 0 rows, detecting the conflict.
expect: First update increments version to 2; second update matches 0 rows and raises conflict.

name: select-for-update-pessimistic
explain: Use SELECT FOR UPDATE to acquire exclusive row locks and prevent double-confirmation in transactional workflows. Use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for lock-free work queues.
steps: Acquire exclusive row lock with SELECT FOR UPDATE to prevent concurrent confirmation. || Query pending work queues with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to distribute jobs across workers without lock contention.
expect: SELECT FOR UPDATE blocks conflicting transactions; SKIP LOCKED bypasses locked jobs immediately.

name: read-committed-nonrepeatable-read
explain: Demonstrate PostgreSQL Read Committed isolation mechanics. Each query acquires a fresh database snapshot, meaning reading the same row twice within an open transaction can return mutated values if another transaction committed.
steps: Open an application transaction and read baseline product state. || Commit a concurrent modification in another session and observe that re-reading within the first transaction yields mutated data.
expect: Read Committed non-repeatable read verified: step1_price=100, step3_price=150

name: queue-lease-vs-selection
explain: Implement durable job queue leases with heartbeat expiration and crash recovery. Tasks become eligible for re-lease if a worker fails to complete before lease expiration.
steps: Atomically claim a queued task with a time-bounded lease. || Recover and reassign an abandoned task after its lease timestamp expires without completion.
expect: Task lease recovery verified: claimed by None, attempts=2

name: async-session-isolation
explain: Demonstrate why async database frameworks (SQLAlchemy AsyncSession) require one session per concurrent task. Sharing sessions across concurrent coroutines causes interleaved statement corruption.
steps: Demonstrate concurrency errors when multiple coroutines interleave queries on a shared session. || Isolate concurrent tasks using dedicated scoped sessions executing in parallel.

name: transient-error-retry-policy
explain: Implement an exponential backoff retry loop with full jitter for database transient errors (serialization failure 40001 and deadlock 40P01). Distinguishes retriable transient errors from non-retriable constraint violations.
steps: Catch transient serialization errors and retry with jittered exponential backoff. || Fail immediately on permanent errors such as unique constraint violations without retrying.
expect: Retry policy verified: transient_succeeded=TRANSACTION_COMMITTED in 3 attempts; permanent_fail_fast=True

name: deterministic-race-barrier
explain: Test concurrent race conditions deterministically using thread synchronization barriers. Synchronizing worker threads eliminates sleep delays and produces 100% reproducible race conditions in automated tests.
steps: Synchronize worker threads at a shared barrier immediately prior to critical section execution. || Release both threads simultaneously to reliably reproduce lost updates in test suites.
expect: Deterministic barrier test verified: expected_serial=20, actual_race=60, lost_update=True

name: idempotency-key-two-phase
explain: Implement two-phase distributed idempotency combining Redis fast in-memory mutexes with a durable PostgreSQL unique ledger. Ensures exactly-once business semantics across server restarts.
steps: Acquire fast in-flight claim in Redis to reject concurrent duplicate requests. || Commit business transaction and durable idempotency record atomically in PostgreSQL.
expect: Idempotent two-phase execution verified: result=confirmed, durable_records=1

name: insert-on-conflict-task-dedup
explain: Prevent duplicate background task execution under concurrent client retries using PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with unique constraints.
steps: Define unique constraint on idempotency_key in task queue table. || Execute atomic INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returning task id, preventing duplicate ingestion runs.
expect: First request inserts task; concurrent retry returns empty RETURNING set and safely reads existing task.
